content.title: Thank you for your review
content.comment:
Dear reviewer, thank you very much for your time and comments.
In this paper, we focused on methods that do not require training data or require only a small sample sufficient for calibration (in contrast with QAT or incremental compression which require data for fine-tuning). That is why the quality of a compressed model is lower than that of state-of-the-art methods which fine-tune models after compression. 
We agree that considering other schemes to choose quantization range might provide benefits and we will try that.
We will use your suggestions to improve our paper for the next submission, including your comments on several notation discrepancies in formulas.

content.title: Thank you for your review
content.comment:
Dear reviewer, thank you very much for your time and comments, and mentioning that previous works on the topic are well covered in our paper.
The novelty of our paper is the introduction of compression technique by proposing an ADMM algorithm with a new type of constraint (eq 6), which allows performing joint factorization and quiantization, which outperforms successive applying of factorization and quantization. And to the best of our knowledge, techniques for joint CP tensor factorization and quantization have not been presented in the literature on NN compression before. In this paper we focused on methods that do not require training data or require only a small sample sufficient for calibration. That is why the quiality of a compressed model is lower than that of a state-of-the art methods which fine-tune models after compression. We will provide more experimental results on other models/datasets for the next revision of the paper, as well as details on the runtime. The layers for fig 2 and fig 3 was chosen as a demonstrative example. Some graphs have too little error among runs to be visible in the plot, we will try to provide more descriptive plots for the next iteration.
We will use your suggestions to improve our paper for the next submission.

content.title: Thank you for your review
content.comment:
Dear reviewer, thank you very much for your time and comments, and mentioning that our method is interesting.
In this paper we focused on methods that do not require training data or require only a small sample sufficient for calibration. That is why the quality of a compressed model is lower than that of a state-of-the art methods which fine-tune models after compression. We compared our joint method to a successive factorization and quantization to maintain the same compression rate. Your comment about scarcity of empirical evidences is fair and we will provide more experimental results for the next revision of the paper. Concerning you question about relaxation of a discrete set - we considered this approach but the resulting method was too time-consuming. 
We will use your suggestions to improve our paper for the next submission, including clarifying the methods section.

content.title: Thank you for a review
content.comment:
Dear reviewer, thank you very much for your time and comments, and mentioning that our method is formulated well and the algorithm used to solve it has a good theoretical support.
In this paper we focused on methods that do not require training data or require only a small sample sufficient for calibration. That is why the quiality of a compressed model is lower than that of a state-of-the art methods which fine-tune models after compression. We compared our joint method to a successive factorization and quantization to maintain the same compression rate. Your suggestion about comparing it to joint pruning and quantization methods is highly valuable - it indeed could provide a fair comparison we were lacking. 
We will use your suggestions to improve our paper for the next submission.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposed a method to jointly do weights decomposition and quantization on a given DNN e.g., resnet.

The problem is formulated as a constrained optimization and an ADMM-based algorithm is used to solve it iteratively.

Experiments conducted on different decomposition rank and quantization bits.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
- The problem is formulated well and the algorithm used to solve it has a good theoretical support.

Weaknesses
- The accuracy degradation is too high and there is no comparison to a different model compression solution: e.g., joint pruning and quantization works or joint neural architecture search and quantization. The accuracy looks not competitive to recent model compression results on ImageNet. It is not convincing that the proposed method is good at compressing models. E.g., compare to results in the joint NAS and quantization [1].
- The baseline of STE-based quantization aware training + weights decomposition should be included as it's the standard solution if people want to get quantized model with weights decomposition on a given DNN.


[1] Wang, Tianzhe, et al. "Apq: Joint search for network architecture, pruning and quantization policy." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2020.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- the problem formulation and algorithm part is written clearly.
- the experiment part is not well designed and important comparison is missing.
content.summary_of_the_review:
- This paper targets on solving joint weights decomposition and quantization problem. The problem is well formulated and systematic algorithm is proposed to solve it.
- However, the accuracy degradation shown in the experiments is too high and far from other DNN joint compression and quantization works. Furthermore, important comparison and baselines are missing in the experiment.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper presents an ADMM based approach to perform low-rank tensor decomposition and quantization on convolutional and fully-connected layers in a neural network. The experiments show that the approach effectively compresses the network with minimal loss in performance.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
## Strengths
1. Performing low-rank decomposition and quantization together is an attractive approach for compression.
2. Experiments show benefits on imagenet with resnet18 network.

## Weaknesses
1. The experiments section is weak as it has results on one dataset with one network and no comparison to any other quantization or low-rank decomposition methods. I would strongly recommend comparing it against other network compression methods to show the benefits of doing low-rank decomposition and quantization together. Also please include the floating point baseline numbers in the tables/captions for better comparison.
2. The method section is unclear and it would be hard to comprehend for a non-expert reader. Specifically, the symbols in Eq. 1 are not explained. It would be better to explain them and their dimensions. Similarly, please include comments and explain the symbols in Alg.1. BTW, is it solving eq. 6 to 7?

## Questions
1. There is a discussion about projecting into a discrete set and the difficulty of optimization. Would it make things easier (in terms of optimization) if the set is relaxed to take the convex hull of the discrete set and gradually make it a discrete one?

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes to approximate weight tensors using a variant of Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM), an optimization algorithm for convex problems. The goal is to lower the error associated with tensor quantization and improve prediction accuracy. A constraint function is introduced to support a joint process of factorization and quantization. A comparison of ADMM against a sequential factorization/quantization process is presented. Results are reported for ResNet18/ImageNet
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- previous works on the topic are well covered, even though the differences against this work are not always clear
- ADMM shows a distinct improvement compared to separate factorization/quantization process it is compared against

Weaknesses:
- the authors original contribution should be spelled out more clearly. It appears to be residing specifically in the use of a constraint function to apply ADMM to neural network layer factorization problems. Is it the actual novelty the introduction of this constraint function that enables ADMM in this context?
- this technique is only applicable to weights, whose compression is generally a much easier problem and less helpful in terms of inference runtime than weight/activations quantization 
- consequently, results are not very impressive, as ResNet18/ImageNet tasks have already been shown to approach or achieve iso-accuracy with INT4 and INT2 weights (better results than the combined factorization/quantization compression factor shown here)
- algorithm runtime is not discussed at all. Is this currently a limitation? How does it scales for networks larger than ResNet18?
- Fig 2 and fig 3 compare accuracy when applying factorization to individual ResNet18 layers or module, respectively. It's unclear what drove the choice of these particular layers to be investigated instead of others, and it is not discussed if some layers are more impactful than others and why.
- In the same figures, it is mentioned that accuracy results are averaged over 3 runs but these graphs don't show errors for ADMM. Do accuracy results perfectly overlapped, even though convergence varies from run to run (as shown in Fig. 1)?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
There are some issues of clarity (especially as it relates to the authors original contribution) and occasional typos throughout the manuscript. The manuscript would benefit from a English revision. Some sentences are really not clear, for example when the authors draw the conclusion that "factorizing with 2x reduction rate and INT4 quantization constraint is more beneficial in terms of memory than INT8 format with 2x reduction rate factorization" (Section 4)

Paper structure could also be improved: convergence results (Fig. 1) are presented before introducing the (single) model on which experiments are run. Table 2 is referred before Table 1 in the text.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper discusses an approach towards weight compression. The authors original contribution is not well defined. Presented results are limited both in scope (a single NN/dataset) and depth of discussion.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper presents a harmonized method for neural network compression by proposing an optimization method that can perform CP factorization and quantization simultaneously. It has been widely known that factorization of a weight tensor and quantization are both helpful in reducing the DNN complexity. The authors' attempt to do both is worthwhile. Experimental results are promising in a few cases when the compression ratio is not too severe.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
+ The paper presents motivations and literature reviews on the factorization-based DNN model compression thoroughly.
+ The proposed ADMM algorithm for simultaneous factorization and quantization is convincing at least in theory. 
+ In some limited cases the proposed methods can achieve compression with acceptable performance loss (2x compression ratio).

Weaknesses:
- Literature reviews on the quantization methods are shallower compared to the factorization-based methods. 
- Performance of the model on critical cases (lower bit depths and higher compression ratios) is unacceptably low. The performance drop compared to the moderate use case (2x compression) is too drastic in these critical cases, while the paper does not attempt to explain much. Basically the proposed method does not work faithfully on high compression cases (4x and 8x), which is too different from factorization-based compression methods' performance reported in the literature. It must have something to do with the joint factorization and quantization of course, but this amount of performance loss is a deal breaker. 
- There might be alternative optimization choices, that haven't been fully discussed or investigated.
    * For example, given the proposed method shows much better performance on a single-module compression scenario, the reviewer wonders if there is any way to perform the transform in an incremental way, e.g., module by module. The paper does not discuss this kind of alternative approaches that could lead to a better performance. 
    * Although QAT can mitigate this issue, but the initial min and max values that define the quantization range in equation 5 as well as the scaling factor induced from them could be defined more carefully; for now they are defined as if the quantization is on the full tensor with no factorization, but I believe they need to be defined for the factor matrices, which are not defined initially of course. There is a discrepancy though and there might be ways to improve this part with a more careful consideration.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is overally clearly written, although there could be some more analysis on the failure modes. 

Some minor questions:
- In eq (6), the indicator functions are defined with infinity. Curious what's the actual choice during training. Does it affect the performance?
- In eq (6) shouldn't B of shape m x r not r x m?
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper attempts to solve a challenging and interesting problem. They do provide a reasonable algorithm that can perform factorization and quantization together. However, the empirical evidence is weaker than it has to be to accept the paper as it is. Needs more investigation and tuning.

content.title: QUANTIZATION AWARE FACTORIZATION FOR DEEP NEURAL NETWORK COMPRESSION
content.TL;DR: We propose a novel approach to neural network compression that performs tensor factorization and quantization simultaneously.
content.abstract: Tensor approximation of convolutional and fully-connected weights is an effective way to reduce  parameters and FLOP in neural networks. Due to memory and power consumption limitations of mobile or embedded devices, the quantization step is usually necessary when pre-trained models are deployed. A conventional post-training quantization approach applied to networks with decomposed weights yields a drop in accuracy. Therefore, our goal is to develop an algorithm that finds tensor approximation directly with quantized factors and thus benefit from both compression techniques while keeping the prediction quality of the model. Namely, we propose to use Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) for approximating a float tensor by a tensor of Canonical Polyadic format (CP), whose factors are close to their quantized versions. This leads to lower approximation error after quantization and smaller quality drop in model predictions while maintaining the same compression rate.
